summary.text: Classical antiquity is the period of cultural European history between the 8th century BC and the 5th century AD, centred on the interwoven civilizations of ancient Greece and Rome.
Conventionally it begins with the earliest recorded Epic Greek poetry of Homer and ends with the fall of the Western Roman Empire in 476 AD.
Its Greco-Roman cultural foundation has been immensely influential on the language, politics, law, philosophy and art of the Western world and, through it, the modern world.

items.prompt: How did Greek culture reach much of Europe during classical antiquity?

options.label: Phoenician traders carried it on their ships
Carthage taught it to the Etruscans
The Romans preserved, imitated and spread it
Alexander's armies settled all of Europe with it

items.explain: The Romans preserved, imitated, and spread this culture throughout Europe.

items.prompt: What helped produce the revival that began in Europe in the 14th century and later became known as the Renaissance?

options.label: Surviving fragments of Greek and Roman culture
A rediscovered Etruscan legal code
The spread of the Phoenician alphabet
Treaties that ended the Peloponnesian War

items.explain: Surviving fragments of classical culture helped produce a revival beginning during the 14th century, later known as the Renaissance.

items.prompt: After the last ruler of Rome was thrown out, what did the Senate vote to do?

options.label: Give the Etruscans a fixed share of power
Crown the ruler's son as the next king
Hand Rome over to the Sabines
Never again allow the rule of a king, and form a republic

items.explain: In 509 BC the Senate voted to never again allow the rule of a king and reformed Rome into a republican government.

items.prompt: Athens led the Delian League after the Greco-Persian Wars and clashed with Sparta's league. How did that conflict end?

options.label: In an Athenian victory that ended Spartan power
In a Spartan victory in the Peloponnesian War
In an inconclusive peace after the Corinthian War
In a Theban victory at Leuctra

items.explain: Athens's dominance in the Delian League led to the Peloponnesian War (431 to 404 BC), which ended with a Spartan victory.

items.prompt: What happened to Alexander the Great's empire after his death in 323 BC?

options.label: It passed whole to his son Philip
It was handed to the Roman Senate
It fragmented and was divided among the Diadochi
It was won back by Persia in full

items.explain: The classical Greek period ends at the death of Alexander and the fragmentation of his empire, which was divided among the Diadochi.

items.prompt: Greek writing had been lost during the Greek Dark Ages. What happened in the Archaic period that followed?

options.label: Written language was revitalized, with democracy beginning
Writing stayed lost until Rome revived it for them
Writing was banned in favour of oral poetry
Writing was kept only for decorating pottery

items.explain: The Archaic period saw the revitalization of the written language, which had been lost during the Dark Ages, along with the beginnings of democracy and philosophy.
